presets.name: drawn (classic)
presets.description:
one group combining its shapes by union (strongest), as a classic drawn
mask did

presets.name: parametric (classic)
presets.description:
one group combining its parametric channels by overlap (smooth), as a
classic parametric mask did

notes: add one parametric channel per property to select on: the mask is strong only where every channel lets the pixel through

presets.name: drawn + parametric (classic)
presets.description:
a "shapes" group, union (strongest), and a "parametric" group, overlap
(smooth), combined by overlap (smooth), as a classic drawn & parametric mask did

notes: mask an area with parametric elements, and refine the selection with drawn shapes
start by selecting the parametric group and adding parametric channels to it, then move on to the shapes group
with overlap operators, only the area where the two groups overlap will masked
use overlap (smooth) if you want their soft edges fading together
use the subtraction operator if you want to exclude the area masked by the shapes instead
alternatively, you can invert the output of the shapes group

groups.name: shapes
notes: draw shapes here to limit the area affected by the parametric channels.
with the union (strongest) operator, the pixels that belong to any of the shapes are masked
change the operator to union (smooth) if you want feathered regions to blend smoothly
use overlap (weakest) if you want to mask only the pixels that are covered by all shapes

groups.name: parametric
notes: add parametric channels here to select the area to mask, e.g., by color and brightness
with the overlap operators, only the pixels that are selected by all parametric channels are masked
change the operator to union if you want to mask the pixels that are selected by any channel

presets.name: mask, overlap and subtract (advanced)
presets.description: a drawn + parametric mask, combined with a subtractive refinement

notes: subtract unwanted spillage from a drawn + parametric mask
start by creating a mask in the drawn + parametric group, then add elements here to clean up the spillage.
